description: LIR is Akatsuki’s longwave infrared camera, imaging thermal emission in the 8–12 μm region to map Venusian cloud-top temperature on both the dayside and nightside.
facility_description: Akatsuki, also called the Venus Climate Orbiter or PLANET-C, is JAXA’s Venus mission for studying the planet’s atmosphere using cameras at several wavelengths and radio occultation.
notes: Descriptions are paraphrased from live ISAS/JAXA instrument pages and the cited papers. DARTS About explicitly directs data users to ISAS Data Policy. Section 6 permits commercial and non-commercial reuse, requires ISAS/JAXA origin credit, asks users to identify and describe modifications, and preserves third-party restrictions. The DARTS acknowledgement is conditional on significant use of its service; general DARTS archive papers are not mandatory instrument citations. Filter files are PLANET-C calibration documents mirrored by NASA PDS. No instrument-specific extra redistribution restriction was found in the inspected inventories, labels or owner pages. No magnitude system is asserted. A24 cached sources were read only; owner and publisher pages were fetched live on 2026-10-26. The PDS label specifies a 7.0° half-cone and incidence columns of 0°, 13.5° and 16.4°. NJM names 10mic_135deg and 10mic_164deg mean 13.5° and 16.4°, not 135° and 164°. Fukuhara et al. Figure 4 is explicitly zero-incidence, so that passband reference is assigned only to 10mic. Taguchi et al. (2023) is a recalibration reference, not a claimed source for all three curves. The instrument paper describes an uncooled micro-bolometer; DetectorType is unchanged.
